subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw make provenance and influence policy a native memory plugin contract, or leave trust-governed memory entirely to external plugins and MCP integrations?
rationale: This choice controls who may assign trust, how persisted claims gain execution influence, and whether every memory implementation must preserve and enforce the policy; repository evidence cannot determine that security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Native shared contract
options.body: Add framework-assigned provenance and influence-policy fields to the memory host contract, with enforcement in the recommended memory implementation and compatibility guidance for plugins.

options.title: External-only policy
options.body: Keep the host contract lightweight and document vetted plugin or MCP systems such as the implementation linked in the discussion for deployments needing governed memory.

options.title: Active Memory only
options.body: Limit the first design to explicit trusted-versus-untrusted Active Memory injection modes without claiming durable cross-backend trust enforcement.

recommendation.title: Native shared contract
recommendation.body: Add framework-assigned provenance and influence-policy fields to the memory host contract, with enforcement in the recommended memory implementation and compatibility guidance for plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and log history directly connect him to the public memory contracts, persisted schema, and retrieval manager where the durable boundary would be defined.
